lines.trans: Here we are, meet my girlfriend.
Hello, I am very pleased to meet you right now.
It is good to meet before the start of our joint work.
Excuse me, did I interrupt you right now?
I came to apologize for my phone call.
I want to say that you are very lucky.

words.gloss: to be lucky (impersonal); to take (by vehicle)

lines.trans: Lyova is the best cook in our restaurant.
He has always been an excellent, reliable sous-chef.
And I am sure he will be an excellent head chef.
Take care of him, and you forgive me, Lyova.
I must respect your desire to leave.
Actually, I was not even planning to leave.

words.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

examples.trans: Quickly copy that number down for yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Прости, я же это не специально.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I did not do it on purpose.

examples.text: Прости меня, Света, но это не ты.
examples.trans: Forgive me, Sveta, but it is not you.

examples.text: Берегите его, и ты прости, Лёва.
examples.trans: Take care of him, and you forgive me, Lyova.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Почему все должны жить по-твоему?
examples.trans: Why must everyone live your way?

examples.text: Я должен уважать твоё желание уйти.
examples.trans: I must respect your desire to leave.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'важать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'respect'.

examples.text: Доброе утро, уважаемая Элеонора Андреевна!
examples.trans: Good morning, respected Eleonora Andreyevna!

examples.text: Шеф, я тебя, конечно, очень уважаю.
examples.trans: Chef, I respect you very much, of course.

examples.text: Я должен уважать твоё желание уйти.
examples.trans: I must respect your desire to leave.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, он дома просто электричество экономил?
examples.trans: Maybe he was just saving electricity at home?

examples.text: Почему твоё заявление с маленькой буквы?
examples.trans: Why does your application start with a lowercase letter?

examples.text: Видишь, всё-таки твоему отцу очень одиноко.
examples.trans: You see, your father is very lonely after all.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'desire / wish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я должен уважать твоё желание уйти.
examples.trans: I must respect your desire to leave.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть желание.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always desire.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.text: Костя, нужно правильно говорить полное здравствуйте.
examples.trans: Kostya, one must say the full hello properly.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, меня зовут шеф Виктор Баринов.
examples.trans: Hello, my name is Chef Viktor Barinov.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, Костя, а где твой папа?
examples.trans: Hello, Kostya, where is your dad?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, тогда уже завтра всё расскажем.
examples.trans: Alright, then we will tell everything tomorrow.

examples.text: Тогда завтра всё расскажем.
examples.trans: Then we will tell everything tomorrow.

examples.text: Напротив, я решил лично поблагодарить вас.
examples.trans: On the contrary, I decided to thank you personally.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

examples.text: Я переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: I am planning to move.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

examples.text: Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave', paired with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Пиши заявление и уходи с кухни!
examples.trans: Write your resignation letter and leave the kitchen!

examples.text: Да я и не собирался уходить.
examples.trans: Actually, I was not even planning to leave.

examples.text: Я ухожу домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('most').

examples.text: Вообще-то я его немного сам доработал.
examples.trans: Actually, I improved it a little myself.

examples.text: Сначала стань сам главным шефом ресторана!
examples.trans: First become the head chef of a restaurant yourself!

examples.text: Хотя я сам отвезу её врачу.
examples.trans: Although I will take her to the doctor myself.
